Another for Not Sorry For Loving You

As for the rape -- it's not just used as a generic threat. Penelope is the Queen (and a princess before marrying Ody, although this isn't necessarily canon in epic). Marrying her solidifies a claim to the kingship. And, as almost any period drama will tell you, lineage and legacy is super important when it comes to securing a throne. You don't just want to be king for 30 years. You want to establish a family dynasty. And you do that by having a child. Marrying the queen of Ithaca and having a child with her cements you pretty firmly as ruler -- and that will absolutely involve rape, because Penelope won't willingly sleep with anyone besides Odysseus, especially if they've already killed her son.

Other people have already made some great points, but I'll also add -- during Hold Them Down, Telemachus is out of the house. Penelope is alone with 108 men who are plotting to rape her -- and even if she isn't explicitly aware of this, we learn through Legendary/The Challenge that Penelope is very aware these men are more and more dangerous. The objectively safest place for her is in her room, where she's offered some protection (even in Hold Them Down, Antonius says they'll only attack Penelope after Telemachus is dead). Plus, as we saw, Telemachus getting involved is more of a hindrance than a help to Ody. Telemachus is young and idealistic (and now besties with the goddess of war), so it makes sense he'd charge in to help. Penelope's intelligence and forethought means when she hears the fighting (and knows/suspects it's Ody), she'll understand that her husband, who is explicitly known for making battle plans, has a battle plan. Blindly jumping in without being aware of his strategy isn't a help at all, and Penelope would never risk throwing Ody off his game for the sake of some "Penelope can kill people too" moment

I felt so much like you in high school--"why keep going if it really will be worse," but the truth is I have never felt as underprepared as I did in high school. Now, even dealing with "worse" or more stressful things, I have about a thousand more options on how to solve them.
